spinach.name: Spinach

sections.whatItOffers: Spinach is a leafy green that cooks down to a small, soft portion rich in folate, magnesium and vitamin K, and it contributes some plant iron.
sections.keyNutrients: See the nutrient list per serving.
sections.howToEatIt: Wilt it into soups, stews, omelettes or pasta, or stir it through warm lentils. A squeeze of lemon or a piece of orange alongside helps your body absorb the iron.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because menstrual blood loss increases iron losses (NIH ODS). Spinach is one plant source of iron, and plant (non-heme) iron is absorbed less easily; vitamin C eaten with it helps. This is general nutrition for anyone who menstruates, not a claim that spinach changes your cycle. If your periods are heavy, it is worth talking to a health professional rather than relying on food alone.

green-lentil.name: Lentils

sections.whatItOffers: Lentils are a filling, budget-friendly pulse that brings protein, fibre, folate and iron in one bowl.
sections.keyNutrients: See the nutrient list per serving.
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer into soups and dals, cool for salads, or fold into grain bowls. Pair them with something rich in vitamin C, such as peppers, tomatoes or citrus; beans and grains contain phytate, which makes minerals harder to absorb, and vitamin C works the other way (NIH ODS).
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because menstrual blood loss increases iron losses (NIH ODS). Lentils supply plant iron, and eating them with vitamin C foods can help. They also provide folate, a nutrient some women of childbearing age do not get enough of (NIH ODS). General nutrition, not a phase-specific treatment. If your periods are heavy, it is worth talking to a health professional rather than relying on food alone.

pumpkin-seeds.name: Pumpkin seeds

sections.whatItOffers: Pumpkin seeds (pepitas) are a crunchy, energy-dense source of magnesium, zinc, iron and plant protein.
sections.keyNutrients: See the nutrient list per serving.
sections.howToEatIt: Scatter over porridge, yoghurt, soups or salads, or blend into a dressing or pesto. A little goes a long way, as they are rich in fat and calories.
sections.cycleRelevance: Magnesium and zinc are part of an everyday balanced diet. We found no reliable evidence tying pumpkin seeds to a particular cycle phase or to relief of period symptoms, so they are here as one tasty source of minerals, not as a remedy. Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because menstrual blood loss increases iron losses (NIH ODS). The iron they provide is plant (non-heme) iron.

broccoli.name: Broccoli

sections.whatItOffers: Broccoli is a green vegetable with plenty of vitamin C and vitamin K, plus folate and fibre.
sections.keyNutrients: See the nutrient list per serving.
sections.howToEatIt: Steam, roast or stir-fry until just tender. Serve it with beans, lentils or other plant iron foods: its vitamin C helps your body absorb the iron from them.
sections.cycleRelevance: Vitamin C improves the absorption of non-heme iron, the form found in plant foods (NIH ODS). Broccoli has little iron of its own, so its role is as a companion to iron-rich plant foods in the same meal, relevant to everyone who menstruates (iron needs are higher for women 19–50, partly from menstrual blood loss). General nutrition, not a phase-specific treatment.

orange.name: Orange

sections.whatItOffers: An orange is a juicy, portable fruit that is an excellent source of vitamin C, with some folate and fibre.
sections.keyNutrients: See the nutrient list per serving.
sections.howToEatIt: Eat it whole or in segments, add to salads, or squeeze over cooked greens and lentils. Having one with an iron-rich plant meal helps your body absorb the iron.
sections.cycleRelevance: Vitamin C improves the absorption of non-heme iron from plant foods (NIH ODS), which is why an orange pairs well with lentils or spinach. Iron needs are higher for women 19–50, partly because of menstrual blood loss. General nutrition, not a claim that oranges change your cycle.
